title: Where Is the Voice Taking You?
headline: After You Fail, Where Does the Next Voice Lead?
headline_sub: Not From the Throne. To the Throne.
tagline: Failure is never God’s signal to run away. It is often His invitation to come closer.
seo_title: After You Fail: Running to God, Not Away (Hebrews 4:15-16) | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Truth always has a direction. A devotional for men on Hebrews 4:16 about what to do after failure: if a thought leads you away from Jesus, it isn't His voice.
verse_text: Let us then approach God’s throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.

scriptures.text: Let us then approach God’s throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.
I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.

items: After every failure…. there is another decision.

blocks.text: The real question becomes: where does the next voice lead?

items: Jesus didn’t simply say, “I am the Truth.”
He first said, “I am the Way.”
God’s truth never leaves you stranded.
The Holy Spirit never exposes sin simply to expose it.
He exposes it so He can lead you home.
That is never the direction of Jesus.

blocks.text: Hebrews tells us that because Jesus understands our weakness, we are invited to approach the throne of grace, not after we’ve cleaned ourselves up, but precisely because we need mercy.

items: The question isn’t simply, “Is this thought true?”
Ask, “Where is this thought taking me?”
If it leads you away from Jesus…. it isn’t speaking with His voice.
Conviction reminds you where weak people are invited to run.
